prediction_question: For a dispatched Austin police 911 call, will a patrol unit reach the caller more than a fixed minutes threshold after the call is dispatched?
prediction_time: At dispatch: the moment the 911 call-taker's ECT screen opens (response_datetime). Only fields known then may be features. Arrival, closing, priority, mental-health, final-classification and injury fields are excluded.
target_definition: Binary: portal column response_time (integer seconds) exceeds threshold T. T is chosen once from the measured training-window distribution and frozen in the construction script before any scoring. Leading choice T = 1200 s (20 min): measured positive rate 0.4008 in the training window (response_datetime < 2025-07-01) and 0.3938 over the full series. Not yet frozen in a construction script.

construction_script: candidates/austin-911-response/source/build.py (stdlib only, runs on a worker; --limit for a bounded coordinator exercise)
construction_output: The runner's layout: public/train.csv, public/eval.csv, private/holdout.csv and meta.json, each split with a SHA-256 in manifest.json. The raw response_time is fetched to derive the label and is excluded from every CSV (see leakage_fix).

leakage_fix.defect: The first version of the script carried response_time into all three CSVs via CARRY_COLUMNS. It was absent from FEATURES, so every declared list looked correct, but the runner treats every non-target column as model input (train.py excludes only id_columns and the target; validate.py drops only the target).
leakage_fix.reproduced_by: reading the emitted header of a bounded build, not the declared lists
leakage_fix.fix: response_time is now LABEL_SOURCE, removed from CARRY_COLUMNS, listed in EXCLUDED_POST_HOC, and recorded in the manifest as label_source_column while being excluded from shipped_columns.
leakage_fix.guarded_by: tests/test_austin_build.py (ConstructedFiles, RunnerContract) and tests/test_qualification_gate.py, which replays the bug and asserts the gate rejects it

qualification.result: the generated extract passes every check the gate is responsible for; only the split-capacity minimums are unmet, because the local fixture is 40 rows per split
qualification.note: The full worker extract has not been built, so its base rates and positive-event counts are still unmeasured. The gate must be re-run on the real extract before any score from it is reported.

split_strategy: Temporal by response_datetime: train < 2025-01-01, eval 2025, holdout >= 2026-01-01. No random split. Measured training window is 572,180 rows, exactly the sum of the measured 2023 (286,145) and 2024 (286,035) counts.

worker_job.status: prepared, not launched - paid launches stay disabled until the scheduled GitHub cleanup run is observed

feature_notes.column_count_note: GET /api/views/e687-fx2y.json lists 25 fields and a resource row returns the same 25 keys with no difference either way. The earlier '42 columns' figure was wrong.
feature_notes.priority_level_reclassified: Documented as 'the priority level assigned to the incident at the time of the first officer's arrival' - post-prediction, so excluded. It had been listed as a dispatch-time feature.
feature_notes.mental_health_flag_reclassified: Documented as settable from the final problem description, the call disposition and a responding officer's assessment - post-hoc, so excluded.
feature_notes.initial_problem_fields_added: initial_problem_description and initial_problem_category are derived from information given to the call taker and were missing from the earlier feature list.

measurements.incident_type_note: All 1,049,636 rows carry the single value 'Dispatched Incident', so the documented exclusion of officer-initiated incidents needs no filter in practice.

response_time_start_offset_measured.conclusion: response_time begins when the 911 call was answered, which is earlier than response_datetime. No column records the call-answered time, so the label start cannot be reconstructed. The target must be the portal column itself, not a recomputed difference.

positive_rate_by_threshold_measured.units: threshold in minutes, value is P(response_time > threshold)

measurements.measured_on: 2026-09-18 via Socrata aggregate and bounded-sample queries; not a scored baseline
